::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
SMIC's smallest of the four 2020-2022 mega-fab JVs (中芯深圳, 55.05% SMIC-owned), a $2.35 billion 28nm foundry with the Shenzhen municipal government.
:::

**Chinese name:** 中芯深圳 (Zhōngxīn Shēnzhèn)

## What does this facility make?

12-inch (300mm) wafers at the 28nm node.

## Why does it matter?

28nm is the workhorse node for automotive, IoT, and power-management chips — the segment of demand China's fabs can serve without needing export-controlled EUV lithography. Chinese industry trade coverage confirms the fab entered production by the end of 2022, on schedule against its original target.

**2.5/5**

## Technology Node Trajectory

- **2015**: 110nm (0.11µm, 8-inch line; commercial production end-2014)
- **2017**: 55nm (first Shenzhen 12-inch/300mm line, ~3,000 wpm)

## Project Timeline

- **Mar 2008** — SMIC Shenzhen entity registered (registered capital $2.415B) — predecessor of the 8-inch line at 坪山
- **Dec 2014** — 8-inch (200mm) line enters production, 0.35µm–90nm
- **Mar 2021** — SMIC and the Shenzhen municipal government announce a $2.35 billion joint venture for a new 28nm foundry
- **Dec 2022** — Fab enters production, targeting an eventual ~40,000 wafers/month
